exposure: premature uterine contractions (PMC) between 24-33 6/7 weeks requiring hospitalization and treatment with tocolytics and/or steroids
cohort: The study included singleton pregnancies complicated with premature uterine contractions between 24-33 6/7 weeks who ultimately delivered at term, compared to a control group of subsequent term singleton deliveries without PMC.
finding: Pregnancies complicated with premature uterine contractions (PMC), even when resulting in term delivery, are associated with adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes, including lower birth weight and an increased risk of neonatal birth-weight <3rd percentile.
mod_finding: The PMC group had higher rates of instrumental deliveries compared to controls.
birth_weight: PMC group: 3149 g +- 429; Control group: 3318 g +- 1.1; also neonatal birth-weight <3rd percentile.
gest_age: PMC onset between 24-33 6/7 weeks; all participants delivered at >=37 weeks.
